entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: | 31st Union Minister of Home Affairs "Minister of Home Affairs (India)") |. | Minister of State in Gujarat |. **Amit Anilchandra Shah** (born 22 October 1964) is an Indian politician who has served as the 31st Minister of Home Affairs "Ministry of Home Affairs (India)") since 2019, the longest-serving holder of the office in Indian history. He served as the 10th president of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) from 2014 to 2020. Shah also served as a member of the Gujarat Legislative Assembly from Naranpura Assembly constituency from 2012 to 2017 and Sarkhej from 1997 to 2012 and the minister of State for Home, Law and Justice, Prison, Border Security, Civil Defense, Excise, Home Guards, Transport, Prohibition, Gram Rakshak Dal, Police Housing, Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs, government of Gujarat in the Modi ministry from 2002 to 2012. Shah was the BJP's in-charge for India's largest and politically most crucial state, Uttar Pradesh, during the 2014 Lok Sabha elections.
